properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is chosen; the options are ideas with their honest counter-arguments beside them, and the road not taken is kept on purpose.

THE PROMPT. I suggested (2026-08-10) that `compare_designs` against the committed export belongs at the OPEN of a session rather than being run when trouble is already suspected, because it was the only thing that found a record diverging from the graph on main. Anthony asked for it to be thought through rather than acted on.

WHAT SEARCHING FIRST DID TO THE QUESTION — it inverted it. The same session then found `fact:correction-the-export-loses-nothing-the-108-were-serialized-defaults`: a 2026-08-08 session ran exactly this comparison, got 108 property-level findings, concluded `export_graph` was silently dropping design, wrote that into a PR body and a handoff note, and retracted it after one probe. They were serialized schema defaults. I had just made the same false claim on the same data, 95 findings instead of 108, without having read theirs. SO THE OBSERVED RECORD OF THIS INSTRUMENT AT ORIENTATION TIME IS TWO RUNS, TWO FALSE DEFECT CLAIMS, TWO RELEASES APART, BY DIFFERENT AGENTS. That is not an argument against comparing; it is an argument that the question is not "when do we run it" but "what does it have to be able to say before running it earlier makes anyone better off".

THE OPTIONS.

(A) DO NOTHING — the null option, and it is stronger than it looks. `where-am-i` ALREADY names `compare_designs` as its first gather step. The failure on 2026-08-10 was not that the step was skipped; it was run, and misread. Adding a ritual does not fix a reading problem, and this project has already rejected the ritual shape twice (`dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written`: build the view, not the document; `dec:read-hint-shape` rejected option B because boilerplate on every return trains the agent to skim). Cheap: costs nothing. Counter: it leaves the actual observed harm — the record was wrong on `main` for an unknown number of PRs and `reflow2_check` is structurally incapable of noticing, since it reads artifact checksums and anchored gaps and never node properties.

(B) COMPUTE IT, DO NOT PRESCRIBE IT — extend `dec:read-hint-shape`'s already-chosen option C (state-derived hint, riding the orientation-shaped reads, fire-on-change) to carry DISTRIBUTION debt alongside coherence debt: "the record and the graph disagree" surfacing at the moment of attention, only when true. This is flo2's F5 filed 2026-08-09 — `loop_status` tracks what COHERENCE is owed and nothing tracks what DISTRIBUTION is owed. Fits the strongest precedent in the design and needs no new vocabulary. Counter, and it is decisive as things stand: a hint that fires on phantom findings is a hint that teaches you to ignore it. Building B before C or D would ship the cry-wolf failure into the one mechanism that currently works.

(C) FIX THE INSTRUMENT — make a property difference able to say WHICH SIDE MEANT IT, so a default never appears as a change. The 2026-08-08 correction already argues this and names the precedent: "a comparison that cannot say which side meant it is the same shape as an edge that cannot say who asserted it (DUPLICATES `basis`, which cost dev_storyflow ten proposed deletions) — the fix there was to make provenance explicit rather than to tune the detector, and the same argument applies." Most expensive; also the only option that makes the finding trustworthy rather than quieter. Counter: property-level provenance is a large surface, and `dec:certainty-derived` would argue it should be DERIVED rather than stored — which may make (D) sufficient.

(D) FINISH BL-198 — "do not serialize a value equal to the default, so an absent property honestly means nobody said". Cheaper than C, kills the noise at its source, and the exporter has evidently begun doing it already (0.25.0 wrote defaults, 0.27.0 does not) while `fact:bl-198` is still listed PLANNED in `epoch:planned-one-write-surface`. Counter, and it is the trap both incidents actually fell into: suppressing defaults does not remove the disagreement, it MOVES it to the transition. Two builds one release apart still differ on every default, and that window is exactly what produced both false claims. So D makes the steady state clean and the upgrade moment worse — which is an argument for D plus a version-aware comparison, not D alone.

(E) WRONG TRIGGER ENTIRELY — the record diverging matters when it is PUBLISHED, not when a session starts. Put the check at export/commit/CI time, where something is about to be shipped, and leave session-open alone. Cheap and well-precedented (`ci-gate` exists). Counter: it cannot catch what is already committed and wrong, which is the case actually observed here; and it inherits the same default-vs-decision blindness, so it would go red on a version bump for no reason.

WHAT IS NOT AN OPTION, said plainly so nobody re-derives it: tuning a threshold so the phantom findings fall below it. That silences the true findings at the same rate as the false ones, and it is the "reduce a SET to a SCALAR" failure this project has already written down.

THE ORDERING THAT FALLS OUT, offered as a finding and not as a decision: C or D before B, and A is a legitimate resting place if neither is worth the spend — because the value of running the comparison earlier is bounded above by the comparison's ability to be believed, and right now it has a 2-for-2 record of not deserving to be.
properties.name: OPEN — should comparing the live graph against the committed record be part of a session's opening move, when the comparison cannot yet tell a default from a decision?
properties.rationale:
Recorded as an open question rather than an answer because the brainstorm materially changed what the question is. I opened arguing for a session-opening step; the design's own memory then supplied a two-instance record of that step producing confident false defect claims — one of them mine, an hour earlier. An idea that is weaker after searching is worth keeping in exactly that state, with the evidence that weakened it attached, so a later session does not re-propose it fresh and pay for the discovery a third time.

Kept deliberately open, and NOT registered as alternatives: each option here is a paragraph, not a design, so `detect_gaps` stays quiet (`undecided_decision_point` fires only on two or more registered alternatives). If one of these grows a design of its own — most likely C, which needs a property-provenance shape — `register_alternative` is what makes it a real fork, and being nudged to choose would then be correct.

The counter-arguments are recorded beside the options rather than used to kill any of them, including against my own opening position. (A) is listed first and honestly rather than as a foil: this project has twice chosen the computed form over the prescribed one, and "the step was already prescribed and was run and was misread" is a real answer to "should we prescribe the step".
